findings.title: Nightly prod→dev sync has failed 4 nights running: scrub.sql's *_enc loop NULLs fleet_proxies.url_enc, which is NOT NULL
findings.evidence: db-sync deploy logs: last success '[sync] done 2026-10-27T04:03:04Z'; on 2026-10-28, -29, -30 and -31 at ~04:0x UTC: 'ERROR: null value in column "url_enc" of relation "fleet_proxies" violates not-null constraint ... CONTEXT: SQL statement "UPDATE public.fleet_proxies SET url_enc = NULL WHERE url_enc IS NOT NULL"'. Prod has 20 fleet_proxies rows (read-only count). 0213 (merged 2026-10-26, v1.364.0) declares url_enc TEXT NOT NULL; scrub.sql blanks every column matching _enc$ generically without considering NOT NULL. Reproduced on a fresh PG18 with all migrations: one fleet_proxies row + scrub.sql in a transaction -> same error. tests/sync-scrub.test.ts never inserts a fleet_proxies row, so CI passes. The job's Railway deployment still shows SUCCESS (the failure only appears in logs), so nothing alerted.
findings.failure_scenario: Every night the restore transaction rolls back (good: dev is not wiped, no prod tokens leak), but dev keeps serving the 2026-10-27 copy of prod: 4+ days of stale data so far and growing; anyone testing on dev against 'real data' (accounting, fleet, Reddit leads 0219 which prod now has) is testing against an old snapshot, and dev's own schema drift (e.g. fleet_cities.pinned dropped on dev only, see A5-02) is no longer being healed. It will stay broken until scrub.sql changes.
findings.proposed_fix: In scrub.sql's _enc loop, handle NOT NULL columns: for fleet_proxies, the sealed URL is useless on dev anyway (dev has no prod FB_POOL_KEY), so either DELETE FROM public.fleet_proxies (fleet_slots.proxy_id and fleet_proxy_checks.proxy_id are ON DELETE SET NULL) or set url_enc to a sentinel the app treats as 'no login' and make the readers tolerate it. Generic option: in the loop, EXECUTE 'DELETE FROM %I WHERE %I IS NOT NULL' when attnotnull, after checking no RESTRICT FK points at the table. Also make db-sync fail visibly (exit code already non-zero — wire an alert, e.g. the uptime-monitor or a Telegram message, on a failed run).
findings.regression_test: Extend tests/sync-scrub.test.ts to insert one row into EVERY table that has a *_enc column (discovered from information_schema, as the sealed-columns check already does), including fleet_proxies, then run scrub.sql with empty search_path and assert it commits and every *_enc is NULL or its row is gone. docs/review-2026-10-31/repro/A5/sync-scrub-fleet-proxies.test.ts asserts the current failure.

findings.title: Migration ledger accepts renamed/deleted files silently; dev ledger holds a deleted migration (0216_fleet_cities_drop_pinned.sql) that would hang the keep-fleet restore
findings.evidence: migrate.mjs only compares files on disk against the ledger; ledger rows with no file are never reported. Dev ledger (read-only): 220 rows for 218 files; extra rows '0216_fleet_cities_drop_pinned.sql' (added 681c2e75 2026-10-27, deleted 8d144721 the same evening, number reused by 0216_fb_pool_cookie_by.sql) and '0056_sell_order_close_reasons_to_check.sql' (renamed to 0057 long ago; prod has the same orphan, so 0057's SQL ran twice there). Dev's fleet_cities has no 'pinned' column; prod and a fresh migrate do. keep-fleet.sql copies dev's ledger into sync_keep._migrations, and sync.sh waits until every one of those filenames is applied again before restore-fleet.sql. No checksum drift on either prod or dev (all 217/218 checksums equal the files).
findings.failure_scenario: SYNC_KEEP_FLEET is currently 0 on db-sync, so today this is latent. If it is set back to 1 while dev's ledger still lists 0216_fleet_cities_drop_pinned.sql (it will until a sync succeeds — blocked by A5-01), the sync restores prod, waits 1200 s for a filename that no longer exists, exits 1 and leaves sync_keep behind, and every later night refuses until someone runs restore-fleet.sql by hand. More generally, renaming an applied migration re-runs its SQL under the new name, and a non-idempotent one would fail backend boot.
findings.proposed_fix: migrate.mjs: log a warning (or fail in CI) for ledger rows whose file is missing. sync.sh/keep-fleet.sql: capture only filenames that exist in the image's migrations directory, or compare against the files list instead of the old ledger. Add a CI check that no migration filename is deleted or renamed relative to origin/main.
findings.regression_test: migration-ledger.test.ts: insert a ledger row for a missing file and assert migrate.mjs warns; CI script diffing `git diff --name-status origin/main -- apps/backend/migrations` for D/R entries.

findings.title: docs/DATABASE.md misses four migrated columns
findings.evidence: Table list matches exactly (90 tables + fleet_minutes view, migrated fresh vs DATABASE.md ERP section). Column-level comparison of the migrated schema against each table's section finds after_sales_cases.currency_code, fleet_hosts.agent_instance, fleet_hosts.agent_daemon, fleet_hosts.agent_seen_at undocumented.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the table reference believes after-sales amounts are always USD (the column note in 0175 still says 'in USD') and computes totals without conversion; fleet agent-instance exclusivity is invisible in the doc.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the four rows to the DATABASE.md tables; correct the amount note for after_sales_cases.
findings.regression_test: A docs check that every information_schema column of a migrated DB appears in its DATABASE.md section (the shell loop used here is ~10 lines).

findings.title: seed.mjs re-run aborts half-way when a bank row is linked to a sell order, leaving a partially wiped dev DB
findings.evidence: 0176 documents that DELETE FROM sell_orders on a linked bank row trips the link CHECKs (sell_order_id SET NULL leaves link_kind/linked_at set). seed.mjs deletes inventory_events and sell_order_lines in committed statements, then DELETE FROM sell_orders without unlinking bank_transactions. Reproduced locally: migrate, seed, insert one bank_accounts + one bank_transactions row linked to a seeded sell order, seed again -> 'violates check constraint "bank_transactions_link_kind_pair"', exit 1, with inventory_events and sell_order_lines already gone.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer who linked a payment on their local DB (or ran the bank sync locally) runs pnpm db:seed; it fails mid-way and leaves orders without lines/inventory history until db:reset.
findings.proposed_fix: Before deleting sell_orders/orders, UPDATE bank_transactions SET order_id=NULL, sell_order_id=NULL, link_kind=NULL, linked_at=NULL (or delete them), and run the whole reset section in one transaction.
findings.regression_test: Integration test: seed, link a bank row to a sell order, run seed.mjs again on the private worker DB, assert exit 0.

findings.title: 0178's NOT VALID check can be validated now
findings.evidence: Prod (read-only): bank_transactions_ignored_unlinked_check convalidated = f; rows violating it = 0.
findings.failure_scenario: While NOT VALID, a future violating row inserted by hand/backfill with the trigger path bypassed is still blocked, but planners and readers cannot rely on the constraint and a later dump/restore into a fresh DB re-creates it NOT VALID; low impact.
findings.proposed_fix: New migration: ALTER TABLE bank_transactions VALIDATE CONSTRAINT bank_transactions_ignored_unlinked_check (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock only).
findings.regression_test: Assert convalidated = true for every CHECK on bank_transactions in a migrated DB.

Not scrubbed by design: users.password_hash. No secret column is missing from the scrub; the defect is A5-01's NOT NULL abort. keep/restore-fleet: logic reviewed (FK-ordered reinsert, ON DELETE emulation for single-column FKs to non-kept parents, identity setval, pool-account match on no+uid); currently dormant because SYNC_KEEP_FLEET=0. One more latent edge: restore-fleet updates fb_pool_accounts.status/holder_name with triggers enabled, so fb_worker_accounts_track (0204) and fleet_fence_pool_owner (0207) fire and record/fence stints for the restored rows — likely benign, not tested. Unindexed FKs remain only on users/warehouses parents with NO ACTION/SET NULL (actor_id, created_by, warehouse_id columns), which are never bulk-deleted; not reported. A targeted vitest run of the repro was attempted before baseline DONE against my own container and errored in harness setup; the psql reproduction is the evidence.
